title: Linear sequences: finding the nth term
examples: How do you find the nth term?
What is the nth term of 3, 7, 11, 15?
What is the 100th term of a sequence?

explain.say: Look at the hops on the number line: 3, 7, 11, 15. Every hop is the same size. A list like this is called a sequence, and each number in it is a term. How big is each hop?

draw.text: Linear sequences: finding the nth term

explain.say: Each hop is 4. That is called the common difference. When a sequence goes up by 4 each time, it is linked to the 4 times table: 4, 8, 12, 16. Now compare it with 3, 7, 11, 15.

items.label: 4th term: 15
items.ask: How do you find the nth term of a linear sequence?

explain.say: Each term is 1 less than the 4 times table. The first term is 4 times 1, minus 1, which is 3. The second is 4 times 2, minus 1, which is 7. Can you see the rule?

items.label: 4th term: 15
items.ask: How do you find the nth term of a linear sequence?

explain.say: The rule for any term is 4n minus 1. Here n means the position: 1st, 2nd, 3rd. Check the 4th term: 4 times 4, minus 1, is 15. It matches the bar!

items.label: 4th term: 15
items.ask: How do you find the nth term of a linear sequence?

explain.say: Fantastic! Now you can jump to any term without counting. The 100th term is 4 times 100, minus 1, which is 399. Wow! Challenge: look at the new hops on the board, 2, 5, 8, 11. What is their nth term?

faq.a: It is a rule that gives any term from its position n. For 3, 7, 11, 15 the nth term is 4n minus 1.

faq.q: How do you find the nth term of a linear sequence?
faq.a: Find the common difference, which goes in front of n. Then work out what to add or take away to get the first term. For 3, 7, 11, the difference is 4, and 4 minus 1 is 3, so it is 4n minus 1.
Put n equals 100 into 4n minus 1: 400 minus 1 is 399.
The amount you add each time to get the next term. In 3, 7, 11, 15 it is 4.
asks: What is the term to term rule?

faq.q: What is the nth term of 2, 5, 8, 11?
faq.a: The common difference is 3, so start with 3n: 3, 6, 9, 12. Each term is 1 less, so the nth term is 3n minus 1.

facts: A linear sequence has the same difference between each pair of terms.
The nth term of a linear sequence has the form an + b, where a is the common difference.

quiz.say: What is the nth term of 5, 7, 9, 11?
quiz.why: The difference is 2, so 2n gives 2, 4, 6, 8, and adding 3 gives the sequence.

wrong.1: n plus 2 only goes up by 1 each time.

quiz.say: A sequence has nth term 3n plus 4. What is the 10th term?

wrong.1: 37 adds 3 instead of 4 at the end.
wrong.2: 17 adds 3 and 4 to 10 instead of multiplying.
